runtimeColors.name: brand
runtimeColors.purpose: A widget's own colour (#rrggbb), standing in for the primary on send and the caret; the launcher wears it too. On the dark composer (#1a2537) it gives way to #f1f5f9 when under 3:1 (forDark). Without one, action-primary shows.

runtimeColors.name: on-brand
runtimeColors.purpose: White or black, whichever contrasts more with the brand (inkOn). Computed, never configured.

runtimeColors.name: mine
runtimeColors.purpose: The visitor's bubble: the widget's colour as it is, in both schemes, because the bubble is not a control.

runtimeColors.name: on-mine
runtimeColors.purpose: The ink that reads on the bubble (inkOn), also its inner 1px edge at 16% and its selection tint at 30%.

chat-page-title.purpose: The h2 of a page in the conversation's place: Projects, a project, Pinned.

code.purpose: The platform's monospace; PF Mono is not available.

greeting.purpose: The launcher's greeting on the host page, in the host's Roboto or system face.

console-body.purpose: The console's text, with tabular figures.

console-card-title.purpose: A station's card and a home panel.

shadows.name: menu
shadows.purpose: The console's account menu, over a 1px hairline ring.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: The console's chat preview; the floating panel uses the light value in both schemes.

shadows.name: hairline
shadows.purpose: Every framed surface: code, tables, charts, the list of chats, console cards.

shadows.name: control-edge
shadows.purpose: Console fields; the chat's composer and name field draw the same edge as a border.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus drawn as a box-shadow: the composer, the comment card, the name field. Elsewhere a 2px outline, 2px off.

shadows.name: focus-ring-host
shadows.purpose: The launcher and the greeting's buttons, on any host page.

shadows.name: station-halo
shadows.purpose: The stepper's current and open station. A halo, never a gap and ring.

motion.name: ease-emphasized
motion.purpose: Panel rise and fade (180ms, 12px), greeting rise (240ms, 8px), launcher lift and return (180ms).

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Background, colour and border changes on hover.

motion.name: found
motion.value: Neutral Fill wash (8px spread) to transparent, 2.4s ease-out, once
motion.purpose: An answer opened from the Pinned page. It does not move, so it plays under reduced motion.

motion.name: upload
motion.purpose: A file card's 2px ink progress line.

motion.name: chart-draw-in
motion.value: 520ms bars, 760ms lines, 600ms washes and slices, cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)
motion.purpose: A chart when it appears or changes kind; none under reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
Three surfaces share one record, and all three are drawn in the PF design language (PFDL 2.3.0, its default Cobalt theme), Intellect's own design system: slate surfaces and inks, one cobalt primary, Roboto, flat surfaces with hairlines. The **chat** is the familiar AI chat window: a white page (deep navy in the dark), answers set as plain text beside the assistant's round mark, the visitor's words in a bubble of the primary colour, a bordered composer field at the foot. It wears the customer's identity in two ways: their assistant's picture (or logo, or initials) beside every answer, and their colour standing in for the primary. It refuses answer cards, brand-filled suggestion chips, a coloured header bar, a second accent, gradients, glass, and a shadow on anything that does not float.

The **launcher and panel frame** sit on someone else's page and take the least room they can: a 56px circle in the widget's colour or filled with the assistant's picture, an optional greeting card beside it, and a 14px-cornered panel in the chat's own ground that rises a short way and fades in. The **admin console** is a working admin in the same language: white cards on a slate canvas with one cobalt primary, in light and dark. The administrator chooses System, Light or Dark; System follows the computer.

Everything is Roboto, self-hosted, at modest sizes and weights; depth is hairlines first, shadow only where something floats.

This is an interim re-skin, and three gaps are known and accepted. The design language's component package (`@purple-fabric/ui`) cannot be installed yet, so each stylesheet writes out the token values at its top (the loader writes them as plain colours) and every part is still the product's own; the names in this document are the design language's token names, so the values can be dropped when the package supplies them. Status words stay capitalised ("Live", "In setup") although the design language writes them lowercase, because the same strings serve as headings and labels. The console's widget column heads its list with one all-caps group label ("Widgets", 12px, 600, 0.04em), which the design language allows for four words or fewer; it is that one heading, not a pattern for other surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: Slate surfaces and inks in every surface (#ffffff cards, #f1f5f9 canvas, #0f172a ink), each with a dark value; one cobalt primary (#0047ab, #3870be in the dark).
A widget's own colour stands in for the primary on the launcher, send, the caret and the visitor's bubble; send gives way to light ink on the dark composer when the colour is under 3:1.
Answers are text, not cards; rich content (code, tables, diagrams, charts) sits in 12px hairline frames that scroll sideways inside themselves.
Roboto throughout, 16px at 1.6 in the chat and 14px at 1.5 with tabular figures in the console; no running text under 12px.
Flat surfaces with 1px hairlines; only the launcher, the greeting, the panel, the "latest message" circle, the console's account menu and its chat preview carry a shadow.
Focus is one ring everywhere: 2px of the focus colour, 2px off.
The chat picks light or dark by the widget's scheme, the console by the administrator's; both write each colour once with `light-dark()`.
Logical properties throughout, so a right-to-left language mirrors.

rules.name: The Stand-In Rule
rules.body: A widget's colour stands in for the primary and goes nowhere else: the launcher, the send button, the caret and the visitor's bubble. Elsewhere it appears only as a trace (a suggestion chip's edge at 55% and fill at 5% under the pointer, and the selection tint at 22%). Never on a header, a background, the mark or a chosen toggle.

rules.name: The 3:1 Rule
rules.body: On the dark composer (#1a2537) a widget colour under 3:1 gives way to the light ink (#f1f5f9) on the send button and the caret, and the ink on it is recomputed (`forDark`). The visitor's bubble is not a control, so it keeps the widget's colour in both schemes, with the ink that reads on it and an inner 1px edge of that ink at 16% for a colour close to the page's own. The console's colour notes use the same line: they warn when the colour is under 3:1 against the light composer (#ffffff) or the dark one, and state the text-on-colour ratio.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean state (live, unpublished, problem) and nothing else. On the Soft Primary Fill a state colour takes a fifth of the ink (80% colour, 20% ink) to hold 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Light Sheet Rule
rules.body: A diagram keeps a white sheet in both schemes, with slate inks and frames; a drawn diagram keeps its source's own colours, which assume a light page.

rules.name: The Pretty Wrap Rule
rules.body: Running text sets `text-wrap: pretty` and anything the customer or visitor supplies wraps anywhere. Code never wraps and table cells wrap only between words; both scroll sideways inside their own frame.

rules.name: The Twelve Floor Rule
rules.body: No running text is set under 12px, in the chat or the console.

rules.name: The Own Frame Rule
rules.body: Content wider than the column (code, tables, diagrams) scrolls sideways inside its own 12px frame, never the conversation. Each scroll region takes keyboard focus with its ring drawn inset. A soft shade shows at an inline edge only while more lies that way (a fixed radial of black at 22%, 12px, covered at each end by a 28px gradient of the frame's fill that scrolls with the content). Rows past the tenth fold behind "Show all N rows"; an expanded table scrolls vertically within `min(70vh, 560px)` with its header held.

rules.name: The Floats Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the thing floats over the page. Nothing that sits in the page (a card, a control, the composer) has one.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus is a 2px ring of the focus colour, 2px off, and that geometry (a gap, then a ring) means focus and nothing else. Where an outline would be clipped or the focus belongs to a whole group (the composer, the chat's name field and comment card), the same ring is drawn as a box-shadow (`0 0 0 2px` of the card, `0 0 0 4px` of the focus colour) with a transparent outline for forced colours; inside a clipped card the outline is drawn 2px inset. On the host page the launcher and the greeting's buttons take 2px of white, then 2px of #1d4ed8, so the ring holds on any page and any colour.

dos: Do read colours, corners and shadows from the design language's tokens (`--surface-card`, `--action-primary`, `--radius-card-lg`, `--shadow-popover`), written out at the top of each stylesheet until `@purple-fabric/ui` supplies them.

Do let a widget's colour stand in for the primary on the launcher, send, the caret and the visitor's bubble, with white or black on it by contrast, and let send give way to light ink on the dark composer under 3:1.
Do set answers as plain text beside the assistant's mark, and the visitor's words in a 14px bubble of the widget's colour with a faint inner edge.
Do keep surfaces flat with 1px hairlines; put a shadow only under what floats (launcher, greeting, panel, the "latest message" circle, the account menu, the preview).
Do give anything typed into the Control Edge (#77879d, #64748b in the dark), not the hairline.
Do draw focus as the 2px ring of the focus colour, 2px off; as a box-shadow on the composer and the chat's small fields; as 2px white then 2px #1d4ed8 on anything drawn over the host page.
Do mark the stepper's current station with a soft halo; a gap and a ring mean keyboard focus.
Do give every colour a light and a dark value, written once with `light-dark()`.
Do let wide code, tables and diagrams scroll inside their own 12px frame with the edge shade, never widening the conversation.
Do start an answer's headings at h2 (18px, 600); the chat's title is the only h1.
Do keep 700 for page titles, the welcome and the home figures; 600 for headings and buttons; 500 for labels, row and card titles.
Do go full screen under 600px wide or 520px tall, with no radius and no border.
Do keep green, amber and red for state alone, and mix a fifth of the ink into them on the Soft Primary Fill.
Do fill a chosen toggle (a thumb, the pin) in Ink; pressed state never takes the widget's colour.
Do open the chat's own small cards (feedback comment, filing, confirmation, files) flat, Raised with a 1px hairline and a 12px corner, and give any field in them the composer's focus.
Do take chart series from the eight series colours in their order, and keep a diagram on its white sheet in both schemes.

Do stop every animation while the panel is closed, and under reduced motion remove the rise, lift, press, spin and greeting animation, keeping only the fade; the dots and sketch bars hold still at 60%, and the found-answer wash still fades because it does not move.

Do give every edge drawn as a box-shadow a 1px `CanvasText` border under forced colours, mark the current chat's row, place or filing option with a 2px `Highlight` outline, give a field that shows focus by box-shadow a transparent outline, and draw an upload's progress line in `CanvasText`.
Do use logical properties, and mirror directional glyphs in right-to-left.
donts: Don't put answers on cards, fill suggestion chips with the widget's colour, or colour the chat's header.
Don't put the widget's colour on a background, header, mark, chosen toggle or border at rest.
Don't add a second accent, a gradient or glass.
Don't put a shadow under a card, a control or the composer.
Don't set text under 12px, or download a monospace face.
Don't use rounded playful type or pill buttons in the console; it is 8px controls and 12px cards.
Don't let text wear a chart's series colours; a series is named by its key.
